newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia importing grain to cover crop shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia importing grain to cover crop shortfall.

text.p: Slovakia is importing 400,000 tonnes of grain to cover the difference between the 1996 harvest and expected domestic consumption until the 1997 crop is gathered, the state reserves authority said on Tuesday.
Earlier, the ministry of agriculture said Slovakia's 1996 grain harvest totalled 3.32 million tonnes, down from 3.49 million in 1995.

"We expected a difference between the (1996) grain harvest and consumption until the 1997 crop, and that is why we had licensed imports of about 400,000 tonnes of grain to cover the shortfall," Peter Haraga, director of the State Fund of Market Regulation, told Reuters.

"We have already imported some 220,000 tonnes of grain, but we have also already signed contracts for the entire remaining amount, so this should not be understood as an offer for any world producer," Haraga said.

The ministry expects Slovakia's annual consumption to be at about three million tonnes of grain this year, of which 0.7-1.0 million tonnes should be used for human consumption and about two million tonnes for fodder.
An unspecified part of each harvest goes to state reserves.
Agriculture Minister Peter Baco said last September that Slovakia would probably import some 300,000 tonnes of grain, including 250,000 tonnes to bolster state reserves.
The 1996 wheat harvest fell to 1.71 million tonnes from 1.94 million in the previous year. The barley crop totalled 0.72 million tonnes, compared with 0.79 million.
The 1997 state budget allocates some 600 million crowns to subsidise grain imports to prevent a price increase of cereal-based products on the domestic market.

"This sum should be enough to cover the difference between prices on the world grain market and the actual price of products in Slovakia, so we do not expect any radical upward movement of these prices," Haraga said.
